technical_terms.how_marx_uses_it: The capacity to work, which the capitalist buys and consumes; distinct from labour itself.
Human action that produces use-values, considered apart from its social form.
The useful quality of a product; produced under capitalism only as the bearer of exchange-value.
The value a product has in exchange, the reason capitalists produce use-values at all.
Determined by the labour expended on and materialised in a commodity, under given social conditions.
Value produced beyond the value of labour-power and means of production, the aim of capitalist production.
The new value created in the process, excluding transferred constant capital.
Instruments and subject of labour, as elements of the process; they transfer their value to the product.
Things the labourer interposes between himself and the subject of labour.
A subject of labour already filtered through earlier labour.
Labour that produces use-values in the labour-process; the term is flagged as not directly applicable to capitalist production.
Consumption of means of production by labour, as opposed to individual consumption.
Capital spent on means of production; its value does not change in production but is transferred.
Capital spent on labour-power; it reproduces its own value and produces surplus-value.
The time that is socially necessary alone counts in creating value.
Labour as expenditure of human labour-power in general, which creates value whatever its concrete form.
s/v: surplus-value relative to variable capital; the measure of exploitation.
Equated with the rate of surplus-value; it says nothing about the absolute amount.
The part of the working day that reproduces the value of labour-power.
The part of the working day in which the worker creates surplus-value for the capitalist.
The part of the product that embodies surplus-value, measured against the necessary-labour part.
Determinable but per se indeterminate; its length varies with surplus labour.
Past, materialised labour (capital) versus the living labour that sets it in motion.
Products as masses of past labour-time embodied in them.
The exchange sphere of buying and selling; surplus-value arises in production, outside it.
The change of money into capital through the purchase of labour-power and production.
Value that expands itself; capital personified in the capitalist.
Commodities of equal value exchanged; the wage is paid at full value, yet surplus arises.
Spinning is treated as simple, unskilled average labour; skilled labour is reduced to multiples of it.
A product with use-value and value, sold on the market.

voice_attribution_risks.note: the capitalist's excuses and his 'practical man' rebuttal are voiced in narration; the irony must not be read as Marx's view
Voltaire's Pangloss line is set as Marx's irony about the capitalist's gain, with the translation in brackets
'gift of Nature which costs the labourer nothing' is Marx's ironic description of the capitalist's view, not a claim that labour is free
a critic of Ricardo's 'Obs.' is quoted and then mocked as a wiseacre; Marx's judgement sits in the same paragraph
'Mr. Carey and other harmonisers' is Marx's irony; the 18% rate is the apologists' figure
Senior's text is a block quote; the 'Apart from efforts in principle' paragraph is Marx's correction; the two must not be merged
dialogue with Senior in second person; 'you' is the professor, not the reader
James Wilson's 'last hour' cry is attributed to him, but its tone is Marx's
the worker's long speech is unquoted; attributing it to Marx would misrepresent the argument
Marx's 'civilised horrors of over-work' is his own ironic label; the Danubian and American cases are his claims
'with true Russian irony' and 'a spirit yet more liberal' are Marx's irony, not the Règlement's words
the Boyard's 'victory' quote is a parody of an opponent, not Marx's own claim
the Quaker defendants' denials are reported as their claims; Marx's ironic framing is in the aside about them
